  {
    "id": "combat-hint-panel-clutter",
    "title": "Permanent instruction wall crowds the lower third and collides with the dual-stick cluster",
    "what": "In every in-bout frame (the 0–0 'LUNGE PUNCH', 'FRONT KICK' and 'IPPON' screens) a full-width dark panel reading 'STANCE ◄ step ▲ jump ► step ▼ crouch / TECHNIQUE ◄ reverse ► forward ▲ high ▼ low' is pinned across the lower-middle of the screen, sitting directly on top of the upper arc of both stick rings so the panel's rounded bottom edge merges with the controls. Its second text row ('► step ▼ crouch') lands over the lighter tatami, dropping contrast, and the whole block plus the two rings plus the 'STANCE'/'TECHNIQUE' labels consumes roughly the bottom 28% of the 844px screen. The panel never clears between moves.",
    "why": "This is the actual gameplay surface. A wall of tiny caps text sitting between the action and the player's thumbs, touching the controls they're reading, is the first thing wrong the moment combat starts and it's wrong for the entire bout — it shrinks the readable action band and forces the eye to parse eight labels while trying to time a punch.",
    "how": "Make the panel a transient tutorial cue, not a permanent HUD: fade it out after the first registered technique on each stick (or after ~4s / on first touch of each stick). If a persistent hint is required, collapse it to a single line of two tiny direction-glyphs hugging the top of each ring, give the panel's bottom edge ≥16px clearance from the ring tops, and lift the lower text row onto the solid part of the panel so it never sits over the bright mat."
